units.sourceHTML: Contributing
units.originalInnerHTML: Contributing

units.sourceHTML:
Like the bird, Wren’s ecosystem is small but full of life. Almost everything is
under active development and there’s lots to do. We’d be delighted to have you
help.
units.originalInnerHTML:
Like the bird, Wren’s ecosystem is small but full of life. Almost everything is
under active development and there’s lots to do. We’d be delighted to have you
help.

units.sourceHTML: The first thing to do is to join the discord community (or the mailing list) and say, “Hi”. There are no strangers to Wren, just friends we haven’t met yet.

units.sourceHTML: Growing the ecosystem #
units.originalInnerHTML: Growing the ecosystem #

units.sourceHTML: The simplest and often most helpful way to join the Wren party is to be a Wren user. Create an application that embeds Wren. Write a library or a handy utility in Wren. Add syntax highlighting support for Wren to your favorite text editor. Share that stuff and it will help the next Wren user to come along.
units.originalInnerHTML: The simplest and often most helpful way to join the Wren party is to be a Wren user. Create an application that embeds Wren. Write a library or a handy utility in Wren. Add syntax highlighting support for Wren to your favorite text editor. Share that stuff and it will help the next Wren user to come along.

units.sourceHTML:
If you do any of the above, let us know by adding it to the wiki.

units.sourceHTML: Contributing to Wren #
units.originalInnerHTML: Contributing to Wren #

units.sourceHTML: You’re also more than welcome to contribute to Wren itself, both the core VM and the command-line interpreter. The source is developed on GitHub. Our hope is that the codebase, tests, and documentation are easy to understand and contribute to. If they aren’t, that’s a bug.

units.sourceHTML: You can learn how to build wren on the getting started page.
units.originalInnerHTML: You can learn how to build wren on the getting started page.

units.sourceHTML: Finding something to hack on #
units.originalInnerHTML: Finding something to hack on #

units.sourceHTML: Between the issue tracker and searching for ⟦CODE0⟧ comments in the code, it’s pretty easy to find something that needs doing, though we don’t always do a good job of writing everything down.
units.originalInnerHTML: Between the issue tracker and searching for TODO comments in the code, it’s pretty easy to find something that needs doing, though we don’t always do a good job of writing everything down.

units.sourceHTML: If nothing there suits your fancy, new ideas are welcome as well! If you have an idea for a significant change or addition, please file a proposal to discuss it before writing lots of code. Wren tries very very hard to be minimal which means often having to say “no” to language additions, even really cool ones.

units.sourceHTML: Hacking on the VM #
units.originalInnerHTML: Hacking on the VM #

units.sourceHTML: The basic process is simple:
units.originalInnerHTML: The basic process is simple:

units.sourceHTML:
Make sure you can build and run the tests locally. It’s good to ensure you’re starting from a happy place before you poke at the code. Running the tests is as simple as building the vm project, which generates ⟦CODE1⟧ and then running the following python 3 script:

⟦PRE0⟧

If there are no failures, you’re good to go.
units.originalInnerHTML:
Make sure you can build and run the tests locally. It’s good to ensure you’re starting from a happy place before you poke at the code. Running the tests is as simple as building the vm project, which generates bin/wren_test and then running the following python 3 script:

$ python util/test.py

If there are no failures, you’re good to go.

units.sourceHTML: Fork the repo so you can change it locally. Please make your changes in separate feature branches to make things a little easier.
units.originalInnerHTML: Fork the repo so you can change it locally. Please make your changes in separate feature branches to make things a little easier.

units.sourceHTML: Change the code. Please follow the style of the surrounding code. That basically means ⟦CODE0⟧ names, ⟦CODE1⟧ on the next line, keep within 80 columns, and two spaces of indentation. If you see places where the existing code is inconsistent, let us know.
units.originalInnerHTML: Change the code. Please follow the style of the surrounding code. That basically means camelCase names, { on the next line, keep within 80 columns, and two spaces of indentation. If you see places where the existing code is inconsistent, let us know.

units.sourceHTML: Write some tests for your new functionality. They live under ⟦CODE0⟧. Take a look at some existing tests to get an idea of how to define expectations.
units.originalInnerHTML: Write some tests for your new functionality. They live under test/. Take a look at some existing tests to get an idea of how to define expectations.

units.sourceHTML: Make sure the tests all pass, both the old ones and your new ones.
units.originalInnerHTML: Make sure the tests all pass, both the old ones and your new ones.

units.sourceHTML: Add your name and email to the AUTHORS file if you haven’t already.
units.originalInnerHTML: Add your name and email to the AUTHORS file if you haven’t already.

units.sourceHTML: Send a pull request. Pat yourself on the back for contributing to a fun open source project!
units.originalInnerHTML: Send a pull request. Pat yourself on the back for contributing to a fun open source project!

units.sourceHTML: Getting help #
units.originalInnerHTML: Getting help #

units.sourceHTML: If at any point you have questions, feel free to file an issue or ask on the discord community (or the mailing list). If you’re a Redditor, try the /r/wren_lang subreddit. You can also email me directly (⟦CODE0⟧ at ⟦CODE1⟧) if you want something less public.
